hypothesis: An independent GF(2) rank oracle and exhaustive signed-edge objective checks will catch parity-cycle or decode/objective mismatches before a parity-QAOA circuit is implemented.
baseline_contract: Existing deterministic classical logical-to-edge parity encoder/decoder and seven-test suite in Batch 073.

combined_contract.graph_family: all labelled simple graphs with 1-5 vertices
combined_contract.cycle_rank: independent GF(2) row rank equals m - n + c
combined_contract.cycle_validity: every declared cycle constraint has even incidence at every vertex
combined_contract.objective: signed-edge preference score agrees for logical assignments, encoded physical assignments and decoded valid physical assignments
combined_contract.degeneracy: component-wise global flips preserve edge parities and objective

dimensions: dimensionless binary variables; graph edge/vertex counts
expected_gain: reduce the risk of implementing a circuit over an incorrect classical mapping contract
falsifiers: independent GF(2) rank differs from the cycle rank or m-n+c
a declared cycle has odd vertex incidence
logical and physical signed-edge objective values differ
a valid physical assignment fails round-trip decoding
component-wise global flip changes encoded parity or objective
resource_boundary: test runtime and host compute will be reported from CI where available; no QPU, energy or cost-per-accepted-task measurement is inferred
rollback: preserve the smallest counterexample and correct the mapping/test before any QAOA circuit implementation
next_gate: pass exact-head Python unit/invariant CI; then implement the higher-order parity-QAOA circuit behind this contract and compare against direct QAOA on frozen held-out graphs with equal shots and optimizer evaluations
